claims.reason: Backed: the 'check whether it is needed' part (art. 12 ust. 6 allows only additional information necessary to confirm identity; UODO says the controller may not ask for more data than necessary and that existing login mechanisms should suffice). Not backed: the 'check the channel' part. Searched both snapshots for an identity document, ID card, channel, scan or secure-transmission advice and found none.

claims.claim: Tekst opisuje przepisy ogólnie, nie jest poradą prawną i nie miał przeglądu prawnika.

scope_gaps.note: Art. 15 ust. 3 (lines 2902-2903) lets the controller charge a reasonable fee for further copies, a fee exception not named in the sentence; the sentence says only 'co do zasady' and names the unfounded/excessive exception.

Art. 12 ust. 3 requires information on the action taken within a month ('w każdym razie'), subject to the extension in the next sentence; a reader could take 'odpowiedź' to mean delivery of the data itself within a month.
Source wording is 'niekorzystnie wpływać na prawa i wolności innych' and it concerns the right to obtain a copy; 'naruszać' reads as a higher threshold than the source sets.

The UODO page in the packet explains only the right to erasure (art. 17); access, rectification, fee, copy and identity points rest on the regulation text alone. The regulation snapshot is the 4.5.2016 publication (line 7); later corrections, if any, are not in it, and currency of the wording was not checked.
UODO's advice to name the right and specify the data is about erasure requests only.
